analysis.title: Global Reflections - 31 Oct 2026 (Nick Savone, Institutional Equity Division sales commentary)
key_insights: Q3 earnings are good but not good enough: 80% of reporters beat EPS and 69% beat on sales as of Wednesday, but the 2.8% median EPS surprise has produced limited positive revisions. Concern is that growth may be peaking as multiples come under pressure.

Hyperscalers are the center of the debate. Microsoft showed strong Azure growth. Alphabet's Google Cloud grew 103% but Search slowed to 12% vs ~14% expected, reviving AI Mode monetization concerns. Amazon's AWS grew 39%, missing elevated expectations, partly on data-center ramp timing.

Amazon backlog is $578B, up ~$80B QoQ, with projected growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028 and visibility into 2029, against $220B of planned 2026 capex. Agentic AI could disrupt Search at Alphabet and Consumer/Retail at Amazon.

Technology had a severe earnings reset over 48 hours. Intel fell nearly 29%, its worst day since 1974, after guiding 4Q revenue down 6% sequentially vs +4% expected, and flagged 2027 as an investment year without positive FCF.

ServiceNow guided 4Q cRPO growth to 18.5% vs ~20% expected while raising its AI ACV target to $1.7B from $1.5B. Reddit reported $895M revenue vs ~$950M buy-side expectations and a 900K decline in US DAUs. Roblox, Pinterest and Twilio sold off on soft growth or guidance. Fortinet fell 21% on weaker services revenue, and Cybersecurity had its third-worst daily decline of 2026.
Semicaps had five straight up sessions through Thursday but remain below their 200-day moving average.

Healthcare and select Consumer held up. Lilly raised FY26 revenue guidance by $5.5B on GLP-1 strength. AbbVie lifted its FY26 EPS guidance midpoint to $13.97. Boeing fell 10% after pushing its $10B free cash flow target out by about a year.

Consumer resilience is selective, with services and experiences stronger than goods. Royal Caribbean beat and raised. Visa and Mastercard cited accelerating US spending, though Mastercard's ~12% 4Q revenue growth outlook was below ~14% expected. Starbucks reported 7.9% North America comps vs 6.9% expected. Floor & Decor cut guidance after quarter-to-date sales fell 3.8%.

Macro: US 3Q GDP grew 3.4% annualized. The Fed held at 3.75-4.0% with two more 25bp hikes expected in December and March. Yields fell on the day, raising the question of whether that reflects inflation confidence or growth and earnings worries.
Thursday was the first day in nearly 40 years of data that the S&P 500 fell while more than 80% of stocks rose. Dispersion is at the 88th percentile of its five-year range.

Hedge fund positioning: summer plus October de-grossing is the largest sustained L/S de-risking in over 15 years. About 35-40% of L/S funds are flat or negative YTD. Americas L/S funds are down ~170bps MTD despite a ~1% S&P gain. Funds are underweight the broader AI trade for the first time since early 2023.

Brazil: Lula won re-election (51.8% vs 48.2%) against investor odds of 80-95% for Flavio Bolsonaro. Local portfolios fell 15-30% over two days and ~$2.5B of futures selling cleaned up tactical positioning.

Asia: KOSPI fell 3.5%, Taiwan 2.5% and the Nikkei 2.1% on Friday as US tech weakness spilled into semiconductors. SK Hynix fell 7.1% despite a favorable memory outlook. Kioxia's ADR fell 17% on a weak December-quarter outlook. MediaTek raised its 2027 AI ASIC revenue outlook to $15-16B. China's CSI1000 fell 8.5% WTD, with suspected state-backed ETF buying stabilizing sentiment.

Europe: the ECB held with a December hike still expected. Homebuilders fell 5.8% after the UK Budget. Standard Chartered beat on pretax profit by 13%, Adyen fell 13% after withdrawing its medium-term margin target, Stellantis rose 15% and Genmab 30%. European gas briefly exceeded EUR100/MWh for the first time since 2022, with storage at 74.9%.

Mike Wilson (MS) sees the mid-cycle correction in its final stages with three clearing events: AI financing concerns, the midterms, and tighter financial conditions. He holds an 8,000 year-end S&P 500 base case, favors quality, and expects semiconductor support around mid-November after possibly another 10-15% decline.

Michael Gapen (MS) expects 25bp Fed hikes in December and March, taking the range to 4.25-4.5%. Unemployment is near 4.2% and wage growth is decelerating. He warns the Fed could need to tighten more if AI investment tightens labor markets.

Midterms: SNAP and Medicaid cuts would subtract 20bps from 2027 real consumption growth, with the baseline slowing from 2.5% in 2026 to 2.0% in 2027. A Democratic sweep would lift 2027 growth only to 2.1% (delay) or 2.4% (broader reversal). Prediction markets price 66% odds of a Democratic sweep.

MS Prime Brokerage data: US L/S net leverage rose 5ppts WoW to 51%, gross fell 1ppt to 207%. Funds covered index hedges and added Memory, Agentic AI, Internet and Cybersecurity, and sold Hyperscalers, Energy, Materials and Real Estate.
MS power research raised its global power consumption estimate by 10% to ~36T units by 2030, with ~$500B of market value to unlock by 2027 and ~14% upgrades to consensus 2028 EPS.
MS European Utilities sees EU power demand at a 2.2% CAGR over 2026-30, with the sector at ~14x P/E, in line with the EURO STOXX 50, and hedge fund net leverage the lowest among European sectors.

MS Latin America Economics sees downside risk to its 2027 Brazil primary balance forecast of -0.7% of GDP, USD/BRL possibly testing 5.50 then 5.60-5.70, and local rates facing another ~100bps of pressure.
MS Chief China Equity Strategist Laura Wang notes MSCI China is down 20.3% YTD, sees another 10-15% downside for offshore indices, and favors A-shares over Hong Kong.

MS Chief Asia Economist Chetan Ahya flags downside to Asia growth if oil stays above $120/bbl, central banks hike further and AI investment weakens in 2027. Korea and Taiwan are most exposed to AI exports.
MS Japan economist Takeshi Yamaguchi expects the BoJ to hike to 1.50% in December and 1.75% in March. The BoJ raised annual equity ETF sales from JPY330B to JPY860B from January 2027.

MS Chief European Equity Strategist Marina Zavolock sees attractive risk-reward for a rebound in European equities, with cyclicals down 13% vs defensives and AI enablers having given up nearly two-thirds of peak relative gains.

earnings_insights: MSFT FY27 Q1 reported: revenue $92.3B (+19% YoY), operating income $45.9B (+21% YoY), both ahead of expectations. Azure grew 48% YoY in constant currency, with guidance of 49-50% next quarter. Gross margin 67.8%, 60bps above consensus.
GOOGL reported: Google Cloud grew 103% and beat revenue expectations by 4%, with an estimated $5B of TPU sales. Search growth was 12% vs ~14% expected.
AMZN reported: AWS grew 39%, below elevated expectations. Backlog $578B, up ~$80B QoQ. 2026 planned capex $220B.
INTC reported: guided 4Q revenue down 6% sequentially vs +4% expected. The stock fell nearly 29%, its worst day since 1974. 2027 flagged as an investment year without positive FCF.
NOW reported: guided 4Q constant-currency cRPO growth to 18.5% vs ~20% expected. AI ACV target raised to $1.7B from $1.5B.
RDDT reported: revenue $895M vs ~$950M buy-side expectations. US DAUs fell 900K vs roughly flat expected.
FTNT reported: stock fell 21% on weaker services revenue.
LLY reported: raised FY26 revenue guidance by $5.5B on GLP-1 strength.
ABBV reported: modest beat, FY26 EPS guidance midpoint raised to $13.97.
BA reported: stock fell 10% after delaying its path to $10B free cash flow by about a year.
MA reported: guided 4Q revenue growth of ~12% vs ~14% expected.
SBUX reported: North America comps +7.9% vs 6.9% expected. FY27 operating margin guided to 13.5-14%.
FND reported: lowered guidance after quarter-to-date sales fell 3.8%.
XOM reported: modest earnings beat, $20B in share repurchases still planned for 2027.
CVX reported: stronger Downstream results and lower capex.

Europe: Standard Chartered reported a 13% pretax profit beat and raised its FY26 outlook. Adyen fell 13% after withdrawing its medium-term margin target despite 23% revenue growth. Stellantis rose 15% on a 3Q beat.
Aggregate: 80% of S&P reporters beat EPS and 69% beat on sales (as of Wednesday), with a 2.8% median EPS surprise. 13% of market cap reports next week.
Kioxia ADR fell 17% on a disappointing December-quarter outlook. SK Hynix fell 7.1% after stronger-than-expected earnings. MediaTek raised its 2027 AI ASIC revenue outlook to $15-16B.
